generatedBy: pnpm gen:example (backend/scripts/example-file.ts): the invented Kleinberg example catchment from backend/scripts/examples/catchments.ts. Synthetic data, no real place or farm.
name: Example · Kleinberg (winter rainfall)
description: Invented demo catchment. Winter-rainfall valley with two tributaries, four fruit and wine farms on drip and micro irrigation with on-farm dams, and two winter transfers from the upper dam, run by priority. The rain gauge has gaps that bias-corrected CHIRPS fills, one flood year is excluded from calibration, and GR4J is fitted to the weir record (Settings → Fit record). Mostly meets demand; the EWR is missed in dry summers.

missing.reason: Observer on leave: the fortnight was entered as 0 mm

calibrationExclusions.reason: Weir drowned in the winter floods: peaks above its rating were not recorded

notes: No highest gauging is recorded for the gauge record (Calibration → Calibration record → Quality flags for Fit automatically, the Highest gauging column), so no day can be flagged as extrapolated: flood days count as readings, however far the rating curve was extended beyond its gaugings.
Of the scored days, 55 days fall in zero-rain runs set aside as missing (Model settings → Rain gaps → Flagged rain); their rain is filled.

notes: The wettest years in the record carry only 1.4× the flow of the driest, so there are no clearly wet years to test on. How the model behaves in wet years is weakly constrained.
